page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.64-512 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. It is powered by dedicated Ampere AmpereOne processors running at a constant clock rate of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 128 physical cores mapping to 128 vCPUs with a single thread per core, accompanied by 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a uniform allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included with the configuration.

This server type does not feature integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Workloads requiring persistent disk storage must utilize network-attached block volumes. The underlying processor topology assigns one physical core per vCPU, mitigating the execution variance and resource contention associated with simultaneous multithreading. However, operational software stacks must support the AArch64 instruction set architecture, and routines dependent on legacy x86 SIMD instruction sets are incompatible.

By delivering high core counts with a standard 1:4 memory-to-core ratio, the VM.Standard.A2.Flex.64-512 offers predictable execution density for scale-out compute. The instance design is suited for high-density containerized microservices, distributed software compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, batch processing, and large-scale web application serving.
